title.value: Bag of Tricks for Fully Test-Time Adaptation
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the top of the paper.
title.quote: Bag of Tricks for Fully Test-Time Adaptation

analysis.description: This research paper presents an analysis of different techniques for Fully Test-Time Adaptation (Fully TTA), aiming to adapt models to data drifts. It categorizes selected orthogonal TTA techniques and evaluates their impact on model accuracy, computational requirements, and model complexity under various scenarios. The study also highlights the synergies that arise when combining different techniques, establishing new state-of-the-art results.

type.justification: The paper describes experiments conducted with various models and techniques to improve Fully Test-Time Adaptation, focusing on classification accuracy and computational efficiency.
type.quote: Our experimental results show that those techniques are already boosting the performance at test time when used alone, but that combining all of them leads to the best classification accuracy compared to a vanilla Tent method and 2 recent state-of-the-art methods on 4 different datasets.

name.justification: The paper primarily focuses on Fully Test-Time Adaptation, a subset of test-time adaptation techniques for adapting models when test and training data distributions differ.
name.quote: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) aims at addressing this problem by adapting a model pre-trained on source data to make better predictions on shifted target data.

name.justification: The paper discusses methods related to test-time training and domain adaptation without access to source domain data, aligning with Source-Free Domain Adaptation (SFDA).
name.quote: TTA shares important motivations and similarities with earlier or concurrent settings that are source-free domain adaptation (SFDA).

name.justification: The paper analyzes the role of various normalization techniques in performance improvement during test-time adaptation.
name.quote: Batch normalization parameters are updated using a combination of the mini-batch statistics and moving averages of these statistics.
